task.name: Schema, migrations, persistence and analytics share one ownership boundary in audit_substrate.py
task.story_text:
## Why

ADR-0008 named `coordinator/audit_substrate.py` as one of the modules whose size is worth reducing,
and recorded that reduction starts by naming the missing boundary rather than by splitting the file.
The boundary here is different from `runner.py`'s and `assignment.py`'s, and saying so precisely
matters because the obvious reading of this module is wrong.

It is 3,173 lines, but it is not a god-function module. It has 85 top-level functions with a median
of 20 lines — the seams already exist at function level. What it lacks is a boundary between four
distinct change-reasons that currently share one file and one ownership:

| layer | evidence |
|---|---|
| schema definition | 8 `CREATE TABLE` statements |
| schema migration | 23 `_migrate_*` functions |
| persistence | `upsert_run_record`, `rebuild_from_runs`, record writers |
| analytics / read model | 28 `SELECT` statements, `derive_observed_cost_cohorts` and 5 other derivations |

These change for unrelated reasons. A new analytical query and a new record migration have nothing to
do with each other, but today they land in the same module, are reviewed together, and collide in the
scheduler as a single file claim.

Some of this size is benign and should stay. A sequential catalogue of 23 migrations is legitimately
long, and splitting it would make it harder to read, not easier — the migrations are meant to be read
in order. The problem is not the line count; it is that storage ownership, migration history, and
analytics share one boundary. An issue that judges itself on lines removed will split the migration
catalogue, which is the one part that should be left alone.

This module also has leverage beyond its own maintenance. It is the substrate every retrospective
question is asked of, including the structural-observer work — a read model that cannot be extended
without touching schema management is a tax on every future analysis.

## Example

Today one module answers four questions, and a change to any of them claims the whole file:

```
audit_substrate.py  (3,173 lines)
├─ 8  CREATE TABLE         schema
├─ 23 _migrate_*           migration history      ← legitimately sequential, leave intact
├─ upsert / rebuild        persistence
└─ 28 SELECT, 6 derive_*   analytics / read model
```

Wanted: storage ownership separated from the analytical read model, so a new query does not touch
schema management and a new migration does not touch analytics:

```
storage      owns connection, schema, migrations, writes
read model   owns queries and derivations, depends on storage through a named interface
```

The questions to settle are where the interface sits, whether the read model may issue SQL directly
or must go through storage, and which of the current derivations belong to the read model versus to
their callers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Storage ownership — connection, schema, migrations, record writes — and the analytical read
      model are separated, with a stated responsibility for each and a named interface between them.
- [ ] The migration catalogue remains a single sequential unit; it is not divided to reduce line
      count.
- [ ] A new analytical query can be added without modifying schema or migration code, demonstrated by
      one such query.
- [ ] Existing audit queries return the same results as before the change, verified against the
      current index.
- [ ] Index rebuild from run records continues to work, including for records written before this
      change.
- [ ] The issue is judged on whether the two layers can now change independently, not on resulting
      file sizes.

handoff.summary: Split coordinator/audit_substrate.py into two modules with a one-way dependency: audit_storage.py owns connection opening/validation, schema, the full 23-function migration catalogue, and every record write; audit_read_model.py owns SELECT queries and derivations. The named interface is audit_storage.AuditConnection — a connection storage has opened, validated, and brought to the current schema — and read-model function signatures are annotated against it. The read model issues SELECT SQL directly rather than routing through a storage accessor (routing would force storage to change on every new question, which is the coupling being removed), and calls storage's _load_migrated when it needs a decoded record so migration stays storage-owned. Storage never imports the read model. The migration catalogue moved as one uninterrupted sequential unit. audit_substrate.py is now a 296-line re-export facade carrying imports and __all__ only, including the private names other modules and tests import (_meta_set, _meta_get, _migrate_record, _load_migrated, _open_validated, and all 27 _migrate_vN_to_vN+1 functions), so all ~20 consumers keep working unchanged. Added verdict_outcome_counts() to the read model as the worked example of a new analytical query needing no schema or migration change. Added tests/test_audit_storage_read_model_boundary.py (51 tests) pinning ownership rather than file size, and repointed three monkeypatch targets that would otherwise have silently become no-ops against the facade.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Storage ownership — connection, schema, migrations, record writes — and the analytical read model are separated, with a stated responsibility for each and a named interface between them.
acceptance_criteria.notes: audit_storage.py owns connection/schema/migrations/writes; audit_read_model.py owns queries/derivations. Each module docstring states its responsibility and what explicitly does not belong to it. The named interface is audit_storage.AuditConnection, documented at its definition and used as the parameter annotation on every read-model query (test_readers_are_annotated_against_the_interface enforces this). Dependency is one-way — test_storage_does_not_import_the_read_model parses storage's AST and asserts no import of the read model. Ownership is enforced by tests, not just prose: the read model is asserted to contain no DDL, no _migrate_* functions, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, no record_*/upsert_* writers, and no sqlite3.connect call.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The migration catalogue remains a single sequential unit; it is not divided to reduce line count.
acceptance_criteria.notes: All 27 _migrate_vN_to_vN+1 functions moved verbatim as one contiguous block into audit_storage.py. test_catalogue_is_contiguous_and_in_order parses the AST and asserts the migration functions occupy consecutive top-level positions with no unrelated function interleaved, and that their versions ascend 1..CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION-1. test_registry_covers_the_catalogue asserts MIGRATION_HELPERS maps each version to the corresponding function object. A future line-count-driven split of the catalogue fails these tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A new analytical query can be added without modifying schema or migration code, demonstrated by one such query.
acceptance_criteria.notes: audit_read_model.verdict_outcome_counts() groups runs by review verdict and landed outcome with run counts and summed cost, over columns audit_records already indexes. It required no CREATE/ALTER TABLE, no _migrate_* entry, and no SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump — audit_storage.py is unchanged by its addition. Covered by four tests including NULL-verdict handling (reported as verdict=None rather than dropped) and the empty-substrate case; one test asserts SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION is unchanged across the query's use.

Step 4 includes test_audit_substrate.py but omits test_audit_schema_guard.py.
  Suggestion: Add tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py to Step 4 and either retarget these internal tests to the owning modules or provide facade wrappers whose dependency lookup preserves the compatibility behavior.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried from plan risk 1 (wide import surface). A re-export facade preserves from ... import X but NOT monkeypatch.setattr(module, name, ...): tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py:522 patches audit_substrate.MIGRATION_HELPERS then calls audit_substrate._migrate_record (line 524) expecting the fake registry to be used, and tests/test_audit_substrate.py:841,876 patch sub._migrate_record. Once the real functions live in audit_storage they resolve their own module globals, so those patches become no-ops and the assertions fail. tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py is not in Step 4's file list.
  Suggestion: Add tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py to Step 4's scope and repoint all three monkeypatch targets at theforge.coordinator.audit_storage; grep for setattr(...audit_substrate before finishing to confirm none remain.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried from plan risk 1: private symbols are imported across module boundaries, not just public ones — src/theforge/cli/audits.py:474 does from theforge.coordinator.audit_substrate import _meta_set, and tests/test_process_teardown_lifecycle.py:784-847 imports _migrate_record. Step 3 says 'explicit re-exports' without stating that underscore-prefixed names must be re-exported too, and a linter or __all__-driven facade would drop them.
  Suggestion: State that the facade re-exports the private symbols currently imported elsewhere (_meta_set, _meta_get, _migrate_record, _load_migrated, _open_validated) with noqa as needed, or repoint those specific callers at audit_storage in Step 3.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried from plan risk 4: 'verified against the current index' assumes a populated .forge run-record corpus exists in this worktree. If it is empty, the before/after comparison silently degrades to synthetic fixtures, which is a weaker check than the AC describes.
  Suggestion: Have the dev record which corpus was used for the before/after comparison, and if no real corpus is available, say so and seed a multi-schema-version fixture set via seed_records (audit_substrate.py:3474) so the comparison still spans migrated records.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The plan specifies keeping audit_substrate.py as a compatibility facade but does not explicitly list the private/internal helper functions (_meta_set, _load_migrated, _migrate_v27_to_v28, and _migrate_record) that tests and CLI modules currently import. Suggestion: Ensure that these functions are explicitly re-exported in audit_substrate.py alongside the public API to prevent breaking existing imports.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
